metadata.title: 1976 Case 32
metadata.original_presentation: A 52-year-old woman was admitted to the hospital because of collapse of the left lung.

required.content: What is the patient's past medical history?
required.response: The patient had mild episodes of wheezing 15 years ago, arthritis in the hips and knees 3 years ago, and severe wheezing 2 years ago. She had episodes of fever and sweats 14 months ago, and a sputum culture showed tubercle bacilli 12 months ago.

teaching_points.content: A history of wheezing and arthritis can suggest underlying systemic conditions. Tuberculosis should be considered in patients with respiratory symptoms and a history of exposure.

required.content: What treatments has the patient received?
required.response: The patient received adrenocorticosteroid therapy for arthritis, and ethambutol and isoniazid for tuberculosis.

teaching_points.content: Adrenocorticosteroids are used for inflammatory conditions, but long-term use can have side effects. Ethambutol and isoniazid are first-line treatments for tuberculosis.

required.content: What is the patient's family history?
required.response: A brother died as a result of tuberculosis 30 years earlier.

teaching_points.content: Family history of tuberculosis can increase suspicion for the disease in patients with compatible symptoms.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Tuberculosis (TB) reactivation or complication
key_features: positive sputum culture for tubercle bacilli
supporting_evidence: History of tuberculosis with positive sputum culture 12 months ago
Family history of tuberculosis
Collapse of the left lung could be due to TB-related complications such as bronchial obstruction or pleural effusion
additional_information_needed: Current chest X-ray or CT scan to assess for active TB or complications
Sputum culture and sensitivity to check for active TB

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Bronchogenic carcinoma
supporting_evidence: Collapse of the lung could be due to a mass obstructing the bronchus
refuting_evidence: No mention of smoking history or significant weight loss
additional_information_needed: Chest imaging to look for masses or lesions
Biopsy if a mass is found

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Pulmonary embolism
supporting_evidence: Sudden collapse of the lung could be due to vascular obstruction
refuting_evidence: No mention of risk factors such as recent surgery, immobility, or history of DVT/PE
No mention of pleuritic chest pain or acute dyspnea

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Pneumothorax
supporting_evidence: Collapse of the lung could be due to pneumothorax
refuting_evidence: No mention of sudden chest pain or dyspnea
No physical exam findings suggestive of pneumothorax
additional_information_needed: Chest X-ray to confirm presence of pneumothorax

required.content: What were the findings on physical examination?
required.response: The patient appeared obese and slightly dyspneic at rest. The left hemithorax was dull with distant bronchial breath sounds, and the right side was hyperresonant with normal breath sounds.

teaching_points.content: Physical examination can reveal signs of lung collapse, such as dullness to percussion and altered breath sounds.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Tuberculosis (TB) reactivation or complication
key_features: sputum culture positive for tubercle bacilli
supporting_evidence: history of TB with positive sputum culture 12 months ago
collapse of the left lung
family history of TB

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Pulmonary embolism
supporting_evidence: sudden collapse of the lung
obesity and dyspnea at rest
refuting_evidence: no mention of leg swelling or pain
no history of recent immobility or surgery

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Pneumothorax
supporting_evidence: hyperresonance on the right side
distant breath sounds on the left
refuting_evidence: no history of trauma or underlying lung disease typically associated with pneumothorax
additional_information_needed: history of any recent trauma or vigorous activity

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) exacerbation
supporting_evidence: history of wheezing episodes
refuting_evidence: sudden collapse of the lung is atypical for COPD

required.content: What were the results of the chest x-ray and tomographic examination?
required.response: The chest x-ray showed almost complete collapse of the left lung and platelike atelectasis in the right-middle-lung field. Tomographic examination showed complete fusiform occlusion of the left main-stem bronchus.

teaching_points.content: Imaging studies are crucial in diagnosing lung collapse and identifying the cause, such as bronchial obstruction.

required.content: What were the findings from the bronchoscopic examination?
required.response: Bronchoscopy revealed complete occlusion of the left main-stem bronchus by apparent extrinsic compression and a white, firm lesion in the right bronchus intermedius.

teaching_points.content: Bronchoscopy allows direct visualization of the airways and can help identify obstructions or lesions.

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Bronchogenic carcinoma
supporting_evidence: complete occlusion of the left main-stem bronchus
white, firm lesion in the right bronchus intermedius
history of smoking is not mentioned but age and presentation are suggestive
refuting_evidence: no direct evidence of malignancy from biopsy or cytology yet

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Tuberculosis
supporting_evidence: history of sputum culture showing tubercle bacilli
family history of tuberculosis
refuting_evidence: patient has been treated with ethambutol and isoniazid
no current evidence of active infection
additional_information_needed: chest CT to assess for cavitary lesions

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Bronchial carcinoid tumor
supporting_evidence: white, firm lesion in the right bronchus intermedius
complete occlusion of the left main-stem bronchus
refuting_evidence: no evidence of carcinoid syndrome symptoms
age is slightly older than typical presentation

current_ideal_differential_diagnosis.name: Sarcoidosis
supporting_evidence: history of arthritis and wheezing could suggest systemic involvement
refuting_evidence: no evidence of hilar lymphadenopathy or other systemic signs typical of sarcoidosis
additional_information_needed: biopsy of the lesion for non-caseating granulomas

required.content: What was the management plan for this patient?
required.response: Ethambutol and isoniazid were continued, and an operation was performed on the sixth hospital day.

teaching_points.content: Continuation of anti-tubercular therapy is important in managing tuberculosis. Surgical intervention may be necessary for obstructive lesions.

final_diagnosis.name: Bronchial obstruction due to extrinsic compression
key_features: Complete occlusion of the left main-stem bronchus
supporting_evidence: Bronchoscopic findings
Imaging studies
